### LASSO Variable Selection

```{r}
# variables
life_satisfaction = wvs["Q49"]
questions <- wvs %>% select(starts_with("Q"), -Q49)

# remove NA values
wvs_clean <- na.omit(cbind(life_satisfaction, questions))

# X as matrix, Y as vector
y <- wvs_clean[, 1]
X <- as.matrix(wvs_clean[, -1])

#split training and test data
set.seed(123)
n <- nrow(X)
train_indices <- sample(1:n, size = round(0.7 * n))
X_train <- X[train_indices, ]
y_train <- y[train_indices]
X_test <- X[-train_indices, ]
y_test <- y[-train_indices]

# LASSO
cv_lasso <- cv.glmnet(X_train, y_train, alpha = 1)
best_lambda <- cv_lasso$lambda.1se
lasso_coefficients = coef(cv_lasso, s = "lambda.1se")

coef_df <- as.data.frame(as.matrix(lasso_coefficients))
coef_df$Question <- rownames(coef_df)
names(coef_df)[1] <- "Coefficient"

selected_vars <- coef_df[coef_df$Coefficient != 0, ]
selected_vars

# he also suggested prediction intervals (maybe meant if we went in the coefficient estimation direction?)

```

### Sensitivity Analyses

```{r}
library(glmnet)
library(dplyr)

# ---------------------------
# helper functions
# ---------------------------
rmse <- function(y, yhat) sqrt(mean((y - yhat)^2))
mae  <- function(y, yhat) mean(abs(y - yhat))

# ---------------------------
# (Reuse your same y, X from above)
# life_satisfaction = wvs["Q49"]
# questions <- wvs %>% select(starts_with("Q"), -Q49)
# wvs_clean <- na.omit(cbind(life_satisfaction, questions))
# y <- wvs_clean[, 1]
# X <- as.matrix(wvs_clean[, -1])
# ---------------------------

# NOTE: fix small bug in your split (you set y_test incorrectly)
set.seed(123)
n <- nrow(X)
train_indices <- sample(1:n, size = round(0.7 * n))
X_train <- X[train_indices, ]
y_train <- y[train_indices]
X_test  <- X[-train_indices, ]
y_test  <- y[-train_indices]   # <-- fix

# Fit CV LASSO once on baseline split
set.seed(123)
cv_lasso <- cv.glmnet(X_train, y_train, alpha = 1)

# =========================================================
# A) Sensitivity to lambda choice: lambda.1se vs lambda.min
# =========================================================
pred_1se <- as.numeric(predict(cv_lasso, newx = X_test, s = "lambda.1se"))
pred_min <- as.numeric(predict(cv_lasso, newx = X_test, s = "lambda.min"))

lambda_perf <- data.frame(
  lambda_rule = c("lambda.1se", "lambda.min"),
  RMSE = c(rmse(y_test, pred_1se), rmse(y_test, pred_min)),
  MAE  = c(mae(y_test, pred_1se),  mae(y_test, pred_min))
)

# number of selected variables + overlap
coef_1se <- coef(cv_lasso, s = "lambda.1se")
coef_min <- coef(cv_lasso, s = "lambda.min")

vars_1se <- rownames(coef_1se)[as.vector(coef_1se != 0)]
vars_min <- rownames(coef_min)[as.vector(coef_min != 0)]
vars_1se <- setdiff(vars_1se, "(Intercept)")
vars_min <- setdiff(vars_min, "(Intercept)")

jaccard_overlap <- length(intersect(vars_1se, vars_min)) / length(union(vars_1se, vars_min))

cat("=== Lambda sensitivity ===\n")
print(lambda_perf)
cat("# vars (lambda.1se):", length(vars_1se), "\n")
cat("# vars (lambda.min):", length(vars_min), "\n")
cat("Jaccard overlap:", round(jaccard_overlap, 3), "\n\n")

# =========================================================
# B) Sensitivity to random split (seed stability)
# =========================================================
seeds <- 1:30

split_results <- lapply(seeds, function(s) {
  set.seed(s)
  n <- nrow(X)
  tr <- sample(1:n, size = round(0.7 * n))
  X_tr <- X[tr, ]; y_tr <- y[tr]
  X_te <- X[-tr, ]; y_te <- y[-tr]

  cv_fit <- cv.glmnet(X_tr, y_tr, alpha = 1)
  yhat <- as.numeric(predict(cv_fit, newx = X_te, s = "lambda.1se"))

  nsel <- sum(coef(cv_fit, s = "lambda.1se") != 0) - 1  # remove intercept
  data.frame(seed = s,
             RMSE = rmse(y_te, yhat),
             MAE  = mae(y_te, yhat),
             n_selected = nsel)
})

split_df <- bind_rows(split_results)

split_summary <- split_df %>%
  summarize(
    RMSE_mean = mean(RMSE), RMSE_sd = sd(RMSE),
    MAE_mean  = mean(MAE),  MAE_sd  = sd(MAE),
    nsel_mean = mean(n_selected), nsel_sd = sd(n_selected)
  )

cat("=== Split sensitivity (30 random seeds) ===\n")
print(split_summary)
cat("\n")

# =========================================================
# C) Sensitivity to privacy: drop "sensitive" variables
# =========================================================
# Replace with actual Q-codes you decide are sensitive (religion/sexuality/politics/etc.)
sensitive_vars <- c("Q260", "Q262", "Q273", "Q240", "Q150")

# keep only those that exist in your dataset
sens_in_data <- intersect(sensitive_vars, colnames(X))
cat("Sensitive vars found:", paste(sens_in_data, collapse = ", "), "\n")

run_lasso_once <- function(Xmat, yvec, seed = 123) {
  set.seed(seed)
  n <- nrow(Xmat)
  tr <- sample(1:n, size = round(0.7 * n))
  X_tr <- Xmat[tr, ]; y_tr <- yvec[tr]
  X_te <- Xmat[-tr, ]; y_te <- yvec[-tr]

  cv_fit <- cv.glmnet(X_tr, y_tr, alpha = 1)
  yhat <- as.numeric(predict(cv_fit, newx = X_te, s = "lambda.1se"))

  vars <- rownames(coef(cv_fit, s="lambda.1se"))[as.vector(coef(cv_fit, s="lambda.1se") != 0)]
  vars <- setdiff(vars, "(Intercept)")

  data.frame(RMSE = rmse(y_te, yhat),
             MAE  = mae(y_te, yhat),
             n_selected = length(vars))
}

# Full model
full_perf <- run_lasso_once(X, y, seed = 123)

# Remove sensitive variables
if (length(sens_in_data) > 0) {
  X_nosens <- X[, setdiff(colnames(X), sens_in_data), drop = FALSE]
  nosens_perf <- run_lasso_once(X_nosens, y, seed = 123)

  privacy_perf <- rbind(
    data.frame(model = "All variables", full_perf),
    data.frame(model = "Exclude sensitive vars", nosens_perf)
  )
} else {
  privacy_perf <- data.frame(model = "All variables", full_perf)
  cat("No sensitive vars matched your column names, so skipping exclusion.\n")
}

cat("=== Privacy sensitivity ===\n")
print(privacy_perf)
# use privacy and interest to conduct sensitivity analyses / check robustness of results
```
